item.title: Book Club: Happy Iceland — Icelandic Canadian Club of Toronto
item.description:
Session Six: FEB 16, 2027 Happy Iceland, Anne Marie Wells, 2026 Non-fiction/Memoir Part memoir, part travel narrative, Anne Marie Wells reflects on her experiences living in and exploring Iceland. Through personal stories, cultural observations, and encounters with Icelanders, she offers an affectionate portrait of contemporary Icelandic life.

item.title: Book Club: Animal Life — Icelandic Canadian Club of Toronto
item.description:
Session Four: DEC 15, 2026 Animal Life, Auður Ava Ólafsdóttir, 2022 Fiction During a snowy Christmas season in Reykjavík, a lonely middle-aged woman unexpectedly becomes connected to a young pregnant immigrant and her child. A tender and often humorous novel about family, belonging, aging, and human connection.

item.title: Food and Tradition on Display at the B.C. Club Bake Sale — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Becky Byerly-Adams This month we explore the Icelanders who settled in British Columbia. Before the holiday season approaches the Icelandic Canadian Club of British Columbia (ICCBC) in Burnaby held their Bake Sale. But it was much more than that. Becky gives us a first hand account of what she experienced attending the Bake Sale. Food can be much more than sustenance. It is a means of preserving one's cultural heritage and identity. When over 16,500 Icelanders emigrated to North America...

item.title: W.D. Valgardson: Interesting Icelander for November 2026 — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Linda Brandson Coates (I558622) This month's review of North American settlements addresses British Columbia, the most western province in Canada. It is here where W.D. Valgerdson calls home. Bill Valgerdson's illustrious career began at a young age. As an accomplished author, poet and teacher, we are grateful for his time with us as a guest of the Icelandic Roots Book Club. His many posts on social media express honest, insightful and respectful narratives that are sometimes personal....

item.title: Snorri 2026: Reconnecting Family and A Heartfelt Thank You — Icelandic Roots
item.description: by Taylor Stevens Snorri 2026 memories bring a big smile to Taylor. He found family he didn't know he had. The experience of living and working with his distant cousin's family on their farm in Iceland gave him a whole new perspective. Taylor's graduation celebrated with the Gimli Viking. Image shared by author. My name is Taylor Stevens, and I am from the town that every West Icelander has probably heard of; none other than Gimli, Manitoba.
